title: Reward progress
summary: Let a brain drive, then give it points for getting somewhere. Points are all evolution can see.

steps.title: Hand the wheel to the brain
steps.body:
The brain named on line 5 is a small neural network. It reads its inputs (three distance rays and the speed) and answers with two numbers: `brain.steer` and `brain.pedal`.

Pass them to `drive` so the brain controls the car. At first its connections have random weights, so it drives badly. Training is how it gets better.

check.message: Call drive with brain.steer and brain.pedal.

hints: Swap the two zeros for what the brain says.

steps.title: A prize for each lap
steps.body:
Training is evolution. Every car gets a score called fitness, and the brains with the best fitness become the parents of the next generation.

Fitness is the sum of the rewards a car collects. Right now there are no rewards, so every car scores 0.

Add a reward of 10 points when `lap.completed` is true. The test drive uses a simple fixed brain that steers away from walls, and it can finish one lap.

check.message: The test drive should score some points.

hints: A reward line looks like this: reward +points when condition.
Replace the comment with reward +10 when lap.completed.

steps.title: Rewards that come too late
steps.body:
Press Check. It trains 40 cars for 8 generations on 30 second runs and reports how far the best car got.

Untrained cars almost never finish a lap, so they all score 0. Evolution cannot tell a car that drove 200 m from one that never moved, so it is picking parents at random. A reward that almost never happens is called a sparse reward.

Give one point for each checkpoint as well. They sit every 10 m, so every bit of progress now counts, and evolution can tell better cars from worse ones.

check.message: Training should get the best car past 300 m.

hints: The car passes a checkpoint every 10 m. checkpoint.passed is true on that tick.
Add reward +1 when checkpoint.passed above the lap reward.
